label: Watched characters
summary: The list of characters shown in the character pool watch window (a debug window).
details: Going by its name and its one use, a list source in a debug GUI file, it feeds the rows of the window. The game does not document its return type.

label: Window title
summary: The title text of the character pool watch window.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla uses it as the text of a label in the debug window's GUI file.

label: This window
summary: The character pool watch window itself, as a value that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name, it refers to the window object. The sample lines the input shows are from other types that also have a Self function; none uses this one.

label: These properties (access)
summary: The character properties entry itself, in the access form the game offers next to Self.
details: Vanilla passes it to the court scene editor's functions that react to finished edits of a description, a locator or roles. Going by the name and these uses, it hands over the entry that is being edited.

label: These properties
summary: The character properties entry of the court scene editor, as a value handed to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses it as the argument of court scene editor functions, for example to toggle an entry open or to ask for its description.

label: This list (access)
summary: The character selection list itself, in the access form the game offers next to Self.
details: The sample lines in the input belong to another type's AccessSelf function. Going by the name, it is the same idea for the character list.

label: Apply filters and sort
summary: Applies the chosen filters and the sort order to the character list.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from the click of a button in the character filter window.

label: Can save preset
summary: Whether the current filters can be saved as a preset.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable or disable a button in the character filter window.

label: Save preset tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that goes with the save-preset button.
details: Returns a string. Going by its name and its use as a tooltip, it likely explains whether or why saving is possible.

label: Clear search text
summary: Clears the search pattern typed for the character list.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from two buttons in the character filter window. The meaning of 'pattern' as the search text rests on the name and on the matching SetPattern function used on text edits.

label: Delete filter preset
summary: Deletes the filter preset given to it.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla passes it the preset row that the button belongs to.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a filter preset entry, such as the row's own item

label: Delete selected preset
summary: Deletes the filter preset that is currently selected.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button in the character filter window.

label: Filters shown
summary: Whether the filter panel of the character list is open, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of a part of the filter window and for the pressed look of a toggle button in the shared list GUI.

label: Finish text edit
summary: Tells the character list that the user has finished editing a text field.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from the 'editing finished' event of text boxes in the character window and the tax collector window. Those boxes set the list's text filter with SetPattern, so the field is a search field; that reading rests on the matching SetPattern calls.

label: Apply preset tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for applying a given filter preset.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla puts it into the 'Apply filters' and 'Select to overwrite preset' tooltips, passing the preset row.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The preset the tooltip is for.

label: Filter category
summary: A named category of filters of the character list, looked up by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a GUI block, with names such as 'age_filter_category' and 'personal_filter_category'. The game does not document the return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the filter category.

label: Filter
summary: One filter of the character list, looked up by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a GUI block, with names such as 'age_filter' and 'adult_filter'. The game does not document the return type.

label: Filter categories
summary: The filter categories of the character list.
details: Going by its name, it returns all categories at once. Vanilla does not use it in any text or GUI file, and the game does not document the return type.

label: Preset name
summary: The name of the filter preset being worked on, as a string.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a label in the character filter window, and compares it with each preset's name to show that preset's button as pressed.

label: Filter with default
summary: One filter of the character list, looked up by name, with a default value for when it has none set.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the marriage, concubine and character finder windows, for example for 'fertility_filter' with the default '(int32)1'. Going by the name, the second argument is that default. The game does not document the return type.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The default value used for the filter.

label: Character list
summary: The list of characters the selection list currently shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model that fills the rows of character pickers in many interaction windows. The game does not document the return type.

label: Matched search patterns
summary: The search patterns that currently match, as a list.
details: Going by its name and its use as a list source in the character filter window, it feeds a row list there. The game does not document the return type.

label: Matching preset
summary: The saved filter preset that matches the current filters.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla never uses it and the game does not document the return type.

label: Load preset warning
summary: A warning text shown with the 'Open Load Filter Preset' tooltip.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla appends it to the tooltip of the button that opens the load-preset window.

label: Save preset warning
summary: A warning text about saving the filter preset.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla uses it as a label text in the character filter window.

label: Saved filter presets
summary: The list of saved filter presets.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of preset lists in the character filter window. The game does not document the return type.

label: Selected preset
summary: The filter preset that is currently selected.
details: Vanilla reads its name (GetSelectedPreset.GetName) for a button text. It is used together with HasSelectedPreset, which tells whether there is one.

label: Selected preset position
summary: The position of the selected preset in the preset list.
details: Returns a pair of whole numbers (a 2D integer vector). Vanilla uses it as the selected index of a list in the character filter window.

label: Sort order
summary: The direction of the list's sorting, as a yes/no value.
details: Vanilla uses it with 'Not' in the sort-by-skill tooltips, to choose between two texts. Which direction yes stands for is not shown by the input.

label: Total characters
summary: The total number of characters in the list.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla compares it with NumberOfShownCharacters in the character finder's count text.

label: Unsaveable filters warning
summary: A warning text about filters that cannot be saved in a preset.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla shows it in tooltips and uses 'is it empty' on it to decide whether to show a warning box.

label: Has filter presets
summary: Whether there are saved filter presets.
details: Going by its name; vanilla does not use it.

label: Has items
summary: Whether the character list holds any character.
details: Vanilla uses it negated as the visibility of the 'scrollbox empty' part in several windows, so what is shown when the list has no entries.

label: Has matching preset
summary: Whether a saved preset matches the current filters.
details: Going by its name; vanilla does not use it.

label: Only inapplicable filters
summary: Whether all set filters are ones that do not apply.
details: Going by its name; vanilla does not use it.

label: Has selected preset
summary: Whether a filter preset is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable a button and to pick the button text in the character filter window.

label: Has search text
summary: Whether there is text in the search edit box.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of a part of the character filter window, likely the clear button. That last point rests on the name.

label: Hide filter presets
summary: Closes the filter preset list.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button in the character filter window. It is the counterpart of ShowFilterPresets.

label: All filters default
summary: Whether every filter of the list is still at its default.
details: Vanilla uses it negated to show the 'current filter' block of the filter window and a warning icon (tooltip about a filter being set) in the multiplayer lobby, and it shows a separate 'all default' block when true. Reading it as 'filters at default' rests on the name and these uses.

label: List is being built
summary: Whether the character list is currently being built, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it negated for the visibility of parts of the diarchy and government administration windows. What 'building' stands for rests on the name.

label: Presets shown
summary: Whether the filter preset list is currently shown.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of a part of the character filter window. It pairs with ShowFilterPresets and HideFilterPresets.

label: Sorting by skill
summary: Whether the list is sorted by the given skill.
details: Vanilla passes a number for the skill: 0 in the diplomacy text, 1 in martial, 2 in stewardship. It is used in the 'Sort by ... Skill' tooltips.

label: Is suggesting
summary: Whether the list is showing suggestions.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it.

label: Shown characters
summary: How many characters the list currently shows.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla compares it with GetTotalNumber in the character finder's count text, to colour the number when some characters are filtered out.

label: Preset name edited
summary: Reacts to the user editing the name of a filter preset.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from the 'text edited' event of the name box in the character filter window.

label: Reset filters
summary: Resets the filters of the character list.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button in the character filter window. That it returns them to their defaults rests on the name.

label: Toggle filters
summary: Opens or closes the filter panel of the character list.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button in the filter window and one in the shared list GUI.

label: Reverse sort order
summary: Flips the sort direction of the character list, going by its name.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from the click of sort buttons in the shared list GUI and the rite creation window.

label: Save filters as preset
summary: Saves the current filters as a preset.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button in the character filter window.

label: Select preset
summary: Selects the preset at the position the user chose in the list.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from the 'selection changed' event of the preset list.

label: This list
summary: The character selection list itself, as a value handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name. The sample lines the input shows are from other types that also have a Self function.

label: Set search text
summary: Sets the list's search pattern from what the user typed.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from the 'text edited' event of the text filter boxes of the court, vassal and religious subordinates lists in the character window, and from the tax collector window.

label: Set preset name
summary: Sets the name under which a preset will be saved.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from the click of a button for an existing preset, passing that preset's name. The same button is shown pressed when the current preset name equals that preset's name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a string, such as a preset's name

label: Show filter presets
summary: Opens the filter preset list.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button in the character filter window. It is the counterpart of HideFilterPresets.

label: Sort by skill
summary: Sorts the character list by the given skill.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from sort buttons in the shared list GUI with 0, 1 and 2, matching diplomacy, martial and stewardship in the sort tooltips.

label: Shown character (access)
summary: The character the character window shows, in a form other functions can use as a data context.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the window's content. The game does not document the return type.

label: This window (access)
summary: The character window itself, in the access form the game offers next to Self.
details: The sample lines in the input belong to other types' AccessSelf functions. Going by the name, it is the same idea for the character window.

label: Claims expanded
summary: Whether the claims section of the character window is expanded.
details: Vanilla uses it for visibility and for the pressed state of the expand button.

label: Diplomacy expanded
summary: Whether the diplomacy section of the character window is expanded.
details: Vanilla uses it for visibility and to choose between two button frames.

label: Modifiers expanded
summary: Whether the modifiers section of the character window is expanded.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of a part of the window.

label: Nothing expanded
summary: Whether none of the character window's expandable sections is expanded.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of a part of the window.

label: Relations expanded
summary: Whether the given relation sections of the character window are expanded.
details: Vanilla passes three relation names such as 'friends', 'rivals', 'lovers' and combines the answer with And and Not for visibility. The exact rule for several names (any or all) is not shown by the input.

label: Titles expanded
summary: Whether the titles section of the character window is expanded.
details: Vanilla uses it for visibility and for the pressed state of the expand button.

label: Traits expanded
summary: Whether the traits section of the character window is expanded.
details: Vanilla uses it for visibility and for the pressed state of the expand button.

label: Unused relation slots
summary: How many slots of a relation type are still empty.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla passes a relation such as 'ward' with 2 or 'guardian' with 1 and uses the result to add that many empty placeholder rows. Reading the second argument as the maximum number of slots rests on those uses.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number of slots shown for it.

label: Can click focus button
summary: Whether the focus button of the character window can be clicked.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable that button.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the character window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from close buttons in the character window.

label: Collapse all sections
summary: Collapses all expandable sections of the character window.
details: Going by its name and the matching AreNoneExpanded; vanilla does not use it.

label: Military strength text
summary: The text for the character's military strength, as shown in the window.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla uses it as a label text. 'Cached' in the name suggests it is stored rather than recomputed each time.

label: Shown character
summary: The character that the character window shows.
details: Used a lot in texts to reach that character's own functions, for example for their name or whether they are a ruler. The game does not document the return type.

label: Children
summary: The children of the shown character, as a list for the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the children rows. The game does not document the return type.

label: Claims
summary: The shown character's claims, as a list for the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the claims rows. The game does not document the return type.

label: Concubines
summary: The shown character's concubines, as a list for the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the concubine rows. The game does not document the return type.

label: Court
summary: The court related to the shown character, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the court part of the window. The game does not document the return type.

label: Court owner
summary: The ruler whose court the shown character is in, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and asks it whether it is valid (IsValid), and passes it to a dread-effect check. The game does not document the return type.

label: Current soldiers
summary: The current number of soldiers, as a whole number.
details: The sample lines are from other types (mercenary company, holy order, hired troop regiment), none from this one. Going by the name, it is the current soldier count; the input does not say whose.

label: Description
summary: A description text, as a string.
details: The sample lines are from other types (building, government type, activity type), none from this one. Going by its name and return type, it gives a description text for the character window.

label: Diplomacy items
summary: The entries of the diplomacy section, as a list for the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of that section. The game does not document the return type.

label: Extra modifiers count
summary: How many modifiers do not fit in the shown row.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla prints it with a plus sign (for example +3) in the character window. Reading it as the hidden count rests on that display and the name.

label: Focus button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the character window's focus button.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla uses it as that button's tooltip.

label: Focus text
summary: A text about the character's focus.
details: Going by its name and string return type only; vanilla does not use it.

label: Grandparents
summary: The shown character's grandparents, as a list for the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the grandparent rows. The game does not document the return type.

label: Legitimacy bar
summary: The legitimacy bar data of the shown character, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the legitimacy bar in the character window. The game does not document the return type.

label: Marriage icon frame
summary: The picture frame number for the marriage icon.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla uses it as the frame of an icon, so the number chooses which marriage picture is shown.

label: Marriage icon tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the marriage icon.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla uses it as that icon's tooltip.

label: Maximum soldiers
summary: The maximum number of soldiers, as a whole number.
details: The sample line is from a mercenary company progress bar, not from this type. Going by the name, it is the upper limit that pairs with the current soldier count.

label: Men-at-arms potential tooltip
summary: A tooltip text about the men-at-arms a subject would give access to.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla adds it to the military strength tooltip under the heading about new men-at-arms if the person were a tributary or vassal.

label: Merit item
summary: The merit entry of the shown character, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the merit part of the window. Merit is a government mechanic; that link rests on the name. The game does not document the return type.

label: Military strength tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the character's military strength.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla uses it as the first part of the military strength tooltip.

label: Next secondary tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the 'next' button for the secondary character.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla uses it as that button's tooltip. What the secondary character is, see GetSecondaryCharater.

label: Parents
summary: The shown character's parents, as a list for the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the parent rows. The game does not document the return type.

label: Previous secondary tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the 'previous' button for the secondary character.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla uses it as that button's tooltip.

label: Relations of a type
summary: The shown character's relations of the given type, as a list.
details: Vanilla passes GetRelation( 'ward' ) or 'disciple' and uses the list for rows and, via GetDataModelSize, for counting them. The game does not document the return type.

label: Relations with empty slots
summary: The relations of a type, filled up with empty entries.
details: Going by its name and two arguments only; vanilla does not use it. The meaning of the arguments is not shown. The game does not document the return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; probably the relation type.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Not documented; probably how many slots to fill up to.

label: Religious subordinates
summary: The shown character's subordinates in their religion, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the window. The game does not document the return type.

label: Secondary character
summary: The secondary character the window currently shows, used as a data context.
details: The name is spelled this way in the game (Charater). Vanilla uses it as a data context in the window, next to the previous and next buttons that step through such characters.

label: Secondary spouses
summary: The spouses of the secondary character, as a list for the window.
details: Going by its name and its use as a list source in the character window.

label: Secondary text
summary: The text that goes with the secondary character.
details: Returns a string. Vanilla uses it as a label text in the character window.

label: Siblings
summary: The shown character's siblings, as a list for the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the sibling rows. The game does not document the return type.

label: Skills
summary: The shown character's skills, as a list for the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the skill rows. The game does not document the return type.

label: Tab item count
summary: How many items a tab of the character window holds.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla passes tab names such as 'family', 'relations' and 'court' and prints the result as the text of the tab button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a quoted name such as 'family', 'relations' or 'court'

label: Timed modifiers
summary: The shown character's modifiers that run for a limited time, as a list.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the modifier rows. 'Timed' rests on the name. The game does not document the return type.

label: Titles
summary: The shown character's titles, as a list for the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the title rows and checks whether it is empty to hide the section.

label: Trait groups
summary: The shown character's traits in groups, used as a data context.
details: Going by its name and its use as a data context in the traits part of the character window. The game does not document the return type.

label: Vassals
summary: The shown character's vassals, used as a data context.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the vassal part of the window. The game does not document the return type.

label: Has liege (even if dead)
summary: Whether the shown character has a liege, counting a dead one as well, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it for visibility, negated together with the court owner check.

label: Has liege title (even if dead)
summary: Whether the shown character has a liege title, counting a dead holder as well.
details: Going by its name and the similar HasLiegeEvenWhenDead; vanilla does not use it.

label: Has next secondary
summary: Whether there is a next secondary character to step to.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the 'next' button and, with HasPreviousSecondary, to show the stepping buttons.

label: Has previous secondary
summary: Whether there is a previous secondary character to step to.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the 'previous' button.

label: Has secondary
summary: Whether the window has a secondary character.
details: Going by its name; vanilla does not use it.

label: Extra modifiers count shown
summary: Whether the extra modifiers number should be displayed.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of the +N label whose text comes from GetExtraModifiersNumber.

label: Relation expanded
summary: Whether the given relation section is expanded.
details: Vanilla passes names such as 'children', 'siblings' and 'grudges' and combines several calls with Or and Not for visibility.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a quoted name such as 'children' or 'siblings'

label: Tab shown
summary: Whether the given tab of the character window is the one showing.
details: Vanilla passes 'family', 'relations' and so on and uses it for the pressed state of tab buttons and other properties.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a quoted name such as 'family' or 'relations'

label: Next secondary
summary: Steps to the next secondary character.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button click.

label: Watch AI
summary: Starts the AI watch for the shown character.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button click in the character window. What exactly watching does is not shown by the input.

label: Click focus button
summary: Reacts to a click on the focus button of the character window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from that button's click.

label: Copy portrait
summary: Copies the shown character's portrait.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it, and where the copy goes is not shown.

label: Watch
summary: Starts watching the shown character.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it.

label: Open barbershop
summary: Opens the barbershop screen.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button click in the character window. What the barbershop shows and for whom is not stated by the input; the word is the game's own.

label: Previous secondary
summary: Steps to the previous secondary character.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button click.

label: Reset tab
summary: Resets the shown tab of the character window.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it.

label: This window
summary: The character window itself, as a value handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name. The sample lines the input shows are from other types that also have a Self function.

label: Set tab
summary: Switches the character window to the given tab.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from tab buttons with names such as 'family', 'relations' and 'court'.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a quoted name such as 'family', 'relations' or 'court'

label: Should show secondary
summary: Whether the secondary character part should be displayed.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of parts of the window.

label: Show marriage icon
summary: Whether the marriage icon should be displayed.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of the icon whose frame comes from GetMarriageIcon.

label: Toggle claims section
summary: Expands or collapses the claims section.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button click.

label: Toggle diplomacy section
summary: Expands or collapses the diplomacy section.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button click.

label: Toggle modifiers section
summary: Expands or collapses the modifiers section.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button click.

label: Toggle relation section
summary: Expands or collapses the given relation section.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from button clicks with names such as 'concubines' and 'children'.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a quoted name such as 'concubines' or 'children'

label: Toggle titles section
summary: Expands or collapses the titles section.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button click.

label: Toggle traits section
summary: Expands or collapses the traits section.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it from a button click.

label: Chat messages
summary: The list of messages in a chat.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla fills the message list of the engine's chat window (multiplayer) from it.

label: This chat (editable)
summary: The chat itself, in a form other functions can change.
details: The sample lines in the input are from other types' AccessSelf functions. Going by the name, this is the same idea for a chat.

label: Chat receiver
summary: The one a chat is addressed to.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla makes it the data context of a part of the engine's chat window, so that part shows the receiver. Who can be a receiver is not described.

label: Receiver name
summary: The name of the chat's receiver, as text.
details: Going by its name and its string return type; vanilla does not use it.

label: Unread messages
summary: How many unread messages a chat has, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in brackets in the engine's chat window.

label: Has unread messages
summary: Whether a chat has unread messages.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the engine's chat window only when there are unread messages.

label: Is room chat
summary: Whether a chat is a room chat, going by its name a chat of a whole room rather than with one person.
details: Vanilla uses it, negated, to show a part of the engine's chat window only for chats that are not room chats. What a room is is not described.

label: This chat
summary: The chat itself, as a value handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name. The sample lines the input shows are from other types that also have a Self function.

label: This message (editable)
summary: The chat message itself, in a form other functions can change.
details: The sample lines in the input are from other types' AccessSelf functions. Going by the name, this is the same idea for a chat message.

label: Message text
summary: The text of the chat message.
details: Returns a string. The sample lines are from a toast message handler, not from this type. Going by its name, it is what was written.

label: Message name
summary: A name of the chat message, as text.
details: Returns a string. The very many uses in the input are GetName calls on other types (activity types, traits), none on this one. The game does not say what name a chat message has (it may be the sender's).

label: This message
summary: The chat message itself, as a value handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name. The sample lines the input shows are from other types that also have a Self function.

label: This notification (editable)
summary: The chat notification itself, in a form other functions can change.
details: The sample lines in the input are from other types' AccessSelf functions. Going by the name, this is the same idea for a chat notification.

label: Notified message
summary: The chat message a chat notification is about.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla's chat notification popup takes the sender's name and the message text from it.

label: Remove notification
summary: Removes the chat notification popup.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when the popup's animation finishes.

label: This notification
summary: The chat notification itself, as a value handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name. The sample lines the input shows are from other types that also have a Self function.

label: Open chat
summary: Opens the chat that the notification is about.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when the chat notification popup is clicked.

label: This chat tab (editable)
